title: Use matrix multiplication
summary: Matrix multiplication combines rows with columns. The inner dimensions must match. It is different from element-wise multiplication.
introduction: Matrix multiplication combines rows with columns. The inner dimensions must match. It is different from element-wise multiplication. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: Matrix multiplication combines rows with columns. The inner dimensions must match. It is different from element-wise multiplication.

blocks.code:
import torch

a = torch.tensor([[1., 2.]])
b = torch.tensor([[3.], [4.]])
print((a @ b).item())
blocks.title: Use matrix multiplication

blocks.text: The result is 11.0 because 1 times 3 plus 2 times 4 equals 11. @ performs matrix multiplication.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Change the final 4 to 5 and calculate by hand.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: Use * for element-wise multiplication and @ for matrix multiplication.
For more detail later, use this [PyTorch further reading](https://pytorch.org/tutorials/beginner/basics/intro.html).
